messages:
maya.k: Heads up — small repro in the node sampleapp: when a request is retried by our client, the request-id header gets replaced with `-` in logs and our DEBUG-level logger falls back to INFO. Happens consistently when the retry backoff hits the 2nd attempt.

sam.t: ugh. can you paste a minimal repro? which SDK version?

maya.k: node SDK 0.13.2 (sampleapp from quickstart). repro steps: set LOG_LEVEL=debug, run `node app.js` and hit /generate with a failing first attempt (I simulated by blocking gRPC for 100ms). Logs show: `level=info request_id=-` on retry lines.

alex.r: could be an OTEL context loss on the retry promise chain — we've seen hooks re-registering samplers and clobbering the trace headers. Any OTEL envs set?

maya.k: only OTEL_TRACE_EXPORTER=otlp and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=sampleapp. I toggled `OTEL_PROPAGATORS` to `tracecontext` and it still reproduces.

sam.t: can you paste the exact log lines? small ones are easier to triage.

maya.k: sure — paste below:
```
2024-10-11T15:22:01.123Z level=debug msg="sending request" request_id=abcd1234 traceparent=00-aaaa-bbbb-01
2024-10-11T15:22:01.250Z level=info msg="retrying request" request_id=- err=ECONNRESET
2024-10-11T15:22:01.450Z level=debug msg="sending request" request_id=efgh5678 traceparent=00-cccc-dddd-01
```

joe.d: interesting the first traceparent is present then later it's different — looks like a new span is created without linking parent. Might be the retry wrapper creating a fresh root context.

alex.r: exactly. The otel hook in the SDK initializes a new trace if it doesn't find context on the callsite. If our retry removes the context from the async chain (eg due to missing `.bind()` or using a bare Promise), the hook will generate a fresh id and our logger's request-id redactor will see no incoming id and emit `-`.

sam.t: quick check: is the retry implemented with setTimeout + new Promise? those are usual suspects.

maya.k: retry is from our http client lib (internal), uses `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, backoff))` inside the catch. I can try switching to nextTick binding.

alex.r: also check OpenTelemetry async hook order in the sampleapp bootstrap. In node, if you init logging before OTEL, the logger's request-id extraction might run with an OTEL shim that hasn't been attached yet. That can hide the request_id until OTEL init completes.

maya.k: good point. bootstrap file currently does: env load -> init logger -> init otel. I'll flip logger init after otel and retest.

sam.t: another quick workaround: keep request id in our own header like `x-rw-request-id` and make the retry code copy it across attempts. That'll survive even if tracing resets.

maya.k: tried flipping init order — now logs keep request_id on retry! Also DEBUG level sticks. So init order looks like the culprit.

joe.d: great find. We should add a note to the sampleapp README and maybe a startup linter that ensures OTEL init runs before logger in the example.

maya.k: agree. i'll open a tiny PR in sampleapp with a startup order comment + a fallback copy in the retry code.

deploy-bot: maya.k opened PR #412: "sampleapp: init otel before logger; preserve request-id across retries" — CI started. :github:

sam.t: ey nice. once CI passes can we add an e2e test that simulates a retry and checks logs for request_id presence? saves future debugging.

maya.k: will add an e2e case. thanks for the quick triage team :thumbsup:
